ai_assessment.method: Full direct Norwegian-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 1372 canonical passages and both titles. Separate subagent drafting from the original preceded review. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported four major and fifty-four minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.63; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: Nora called herself ‘mẹ’ to the nurse Anne-Marie, who raised her; the pair is ‘con/vú’, and ‘mẹ’ is kept only toward her own children.
Krogstad’s ‘tas til nåde igjen’ was rendered in garbled Vietnamese; corrected.
‘Romansproget’ (the language of novels) was rendered as ‘Romance languages’; corrected, and the Capripike pun tightened.
‘Farvel’ was rendered ‘Vĩnh biệt’ (farewell for ever) in Nora’s last word and in units 1204 and 1347, adding a finality the Norwegian lacks; now ‘Từ biệt’.
Rank’s ‘fru Helmer’ was ‘cô Nora’ here and ‘cô Helmer’ elsewhere; unified as ‘cô Helmer’.
‘Vinkelskriver’ was rendered two ways; unified as ‘thầy cãi lậu’.
The corrected rendering of ‘tas til nåde igjen’ still sounds slightly lordly.
‘Vợ và chồng’ reverses ‘mann og kone’ against the anh/tôi order.
The stage direction for the slamming door is a little awkward.

summary: Full assessment of all 1,372 Norwegian/Vietnamese passages: the cast list, three act headings, every speech and every stage direction, translated directly from the Norwegian Wikisource transcription. The first reviews of six ranges scored 8.85, 8.58, 8.80, 8.63, 8.30 and 8.63 and found four majors (Nora’s ‘mẹ’ to her nurse, a garbled threat of Krogstad’s, ‘romansproget’ read as Romance languages, and ‘farewell for ever’ added to Nora’s farewells); one round of fixes and fresh separate-context blind reviews of the four ranges with majors then scored 9.05, 8.85, 8.80 and 8.80, with the two ranges that had passed (8.85 and 8.80) given a minors-only polish, and no major or critical finding open. The final score is taken from the weakest range, 8.80 on the half-point scale, above the unchanged 8.6 threshold. Open minors include a slightly lordly rendering in unit 842, a reversed ‘vợ và chồng’ in unit 1259 and an awkward closing stage direction.

title_review.rationale: The title is translated as ‘Ngôi nhà búp bê’; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.
